trip.title: Switzerland
assumptions: Every traveller holds a Swiss Half Fare Card (CHF 150 each, valid one calendar month, bought to cover 4-13 September).
Flights are booked. Four land at Zurich on Friday 4 September at 20:30, the fifth on Saturday 5 September at 06:30, and all five leave for Tel Aviv on Sunday 13 September at 11:45.

Three things are booked and fixed: the first night at the Zleep Hotel in Kloten, the Historical apartment in Schwyz for 5-7 September, and the van - a 7-seat VW Caddy from Europcar, collected Saturday 5 September at 09:00 and returned Friday 11 September at 12:00, seven days at ILS 1,505, about CHF 414.

The Jungfrau base for 7-11 September is not booked yet. The plan below is built on Grindelwald village, where Chalet Adelheid leads at CHF 1,356 for the four nights. The fallback held in reserve is LaVida Peak at Reichenbach im Kandertal, CHF 1,474 with free cancellation - a lovely apartment in the wrong valley, which costs about three and a half hours of extra driving across the block and a 06:40 start on Jungfraujoch morning.

Two accommodation figures are estimates until the confirmations are read: the Zleep night on the 4th, and the Kloten rooms for 11-13 September. Everything else is a published 2026 tariff or a quoted rate.

Fares are the operators' published 2026 tariffs, verified in August 2026 against Jungfraubahnen, Schilthornbahn, Rigi Bahnen, SGV, Aareschlucht AG, Oeschinensee AG and the Titlis and Niesen operators.
At five people a 7-seat MPV works: the back row folds flat for luggage. At six it would not have.

trip_wide_costs.note: Buy before departure. It halves almost every fare in this plan, and on the Niesen and the Engstligenalp it beats the senior tariff outright.

Booked with Europcar at ILS 1,505. Collected Saturday 5 September at 09:00, returned Friday the 11th at 12:00. A noon collection would have billed six days at CHF 380, so the seventh day cost CHF 35 and bought a whole morning.

trip_wide_costs.item: Fuel, approx 525 km, plus the top-up before the airport
trip_wide_costs.note: The hire is full to full. Refuel in Kloten town on the last morning, never at a motorway services. The vignette comes fitted on Swiss rentals - confirm it is the 2026 one.

trip_wide_costs.item: Food beyond the two big shops
trip_wide_costs.note: Self-catered breakfasts and lunches, four dinners out for five at Swiss restaurant prices. Parking at Weggis, Lungern and Lauterbrunnen is costed on its own day; Grindelwald comes with the apartment.

days.title: Land at Zurich, sleep in Kloten
days.movement: Land at 20:30, four of the five. Passport control and bags, then the short hop to the hotel in Kloten. No van tonight - the hire does not start until nine tomorrow morning, so nobody drives on the evening they land.

group.item: Zleep Hotel Kloten, rooms for four

tips: Only four beds are needed tonight. The fifth traveller lands at 06:30 tomorrow morning.
Zurich is one hour behind Tel Aviv in September, so there is no jet lag to fight - only the flights themselves.
The Zleep figure here is an estimate until the confirmation is read. Replace it with the booked rate.
Pack tomorrow's driving day tonight. The van is collected at 09:00 and the fifth traveller arrives at 06:30, so the morning has no slack in it.

days.title: Collect the van, cross to Zug, and settle in Schwyz
days.sleep: Schwyz (the Historical apartment, night 1 of 2, booked)
days.movement: Back to the terminal for the 06:30 arrival - allow until about 07:15 for passport control and bags. The van comes from the Rental Centre at 09:00. Then the A4 south past the Zugersee: Zug for late morning, Schwyz by about 13:15. Check-in is 16:00 by key box, so the middle of the afternoon belongs to Brunnen, five minutes down the road.
days.parents: Zug's lakefront and old town are flat, paved and full of benches, and the Zytturm is better looked at than climbed. Then the promenade at Brunnen, where the lake turns the corner into the Urnersee and the mountains close in on both sides.
days.adults: Climb the Zytturm for the roofs and the lake, then swim off the Brunnen lido - the water is still warm in the first week of September.
tips: Do the big shop TODAY. Tomorrow is Sunday and Swiss supermarkets shut - the Coop and Migros in Schwyz close around 17:00 on a Saturday and do not open again until Monday.
Check-in at the apartment is 16:00 and it is self check-in by key box, so there is no desk to reach and no reason to hurry back before four.
Zug's Kirschtorte is the real thing here, not a tourist confection - the Speck bakery on Alpenstrasse invented it in 1915.
Brunnen is five minutes from the apartment, and the view down the Urnersee from the quay is the one on all the old posters. Go at the end of the afternoon, when the light comes down the lake.
Do not take the van into Zug's old town. Use the Postplatz or Casino garages and walk in - it is pedestrianised anyway.

days.title: Mount Rigi from Weggis, and Lucerne at dusk
days.sleep: Schwyz (the Historical apartment, night 2 of 2, booked)
days.movement: Drive round the lake to Weggis, about half an hour, and park at the pier. Cable car up to Rigi Kaltbad, then the cog railway to Rigi Kulm. Come down the same way, or walk the 4 km from Kulm to Kaltbad. The van waits at the pier all day, so the late afternoon is the boat across to Lucerne and the 19:12 back.
days.parents: Cable car and cog railway to the summit, the flat panorama terrace and the restaurant at the top. Down exactly the way you came up - there is no walking in this day at all unless you want it. In Lucerne, the Chapel Bridge, the waterfront and the Old Town squares are all level.
days.adults: Walk Rigi Kulm down to Kaltbad: 4 km, about an hour and a quarter, a wide easy track with the whole of Lake Lucerne underneath you the entire way. In Lucerne, add the Musegg Wall towers, which are stairs.
tips: The last boat back from Lucerne leaves at 19:12 and reaches Weggis at 19:53. Miss it and it is train plus bus, 51 minutes, CHF 5.20 - not a disaster, but the van is at the pier and the boat is the nicer end to the day.
See the Chapel Bridge in the early evening rather than at midday. That is what this day is shaped around.
Rigi Kulm is 1,798 m and the terrace is exposed. Take a layer even if Weggis is warm.
Weggis parking is CHF 13 for 24 hours and it is not free, whatever the village website implies.
If Rigi is in cloud, do not go up. Take the boat down to Flüelen instead and the train back - three hours through the dramatic far end of the lake, all of it seated.
Everything is shut today except restaurants and the stations. This is the whole reason the big shop happened yesterday.

days.title: Over the Brünig to the Jungfrau, by way of Lungern and the Aare Gorge
days.movement: Schwyz to Lucerne on the A4, then the A2 and A8 south through Sarnen and Giswil. Stop at Lungern for the lake and, if the morning is clear, the Turren cable car. Over the Brünig, then fifteen minutes off the road at Meiringen for the Aare Gorge. Back through Brienz and Interlaken to Wilderswil, Zweilütschinen and Grindelwald. About 145 km and two and a half hours of driving, four and a half door to door with both stops.
days.parents: The lakeside path at Lungern-Obsee is flat and paved with a restaurant at each end. At the gorge, go in from the WEST entrance: the first half, as far as the middle, is level, railed and passable with a wheelchair or a narrow pushchair, and the operator calls it the most beautiful part anyway.
days.adults: Add the Turren cable car above Lungern - ten minutes to a terrace facing the Bernese Alps across the lake - and walk the full 1.4 km of the gorge to the east end, about 45 minutes.

per_person.item: Lungern-Turren cable car return, half fare

group.item: Grindelwald apartment + visitor's tax, night 1 of 4

tips: The Aare Gorge is CHF 13 a head in 2026, not the CHF 10 that half the internet still quotes. Parking at the West entrance is free and takes a van.
Both gorge entrances stay open until 18:30 through 20 September, after which it drops to 17:30. There is plenty of margin for a mid-afternoon arrival.

Do NOT pull into the Chälrütirank viewpoint above Lungern with a seven-seater. It is an unmarked pull-in on a wide bend with a handful of spaces and coaches fill it. Use the Obsee car park instead - 222 spaces, CHF 5 for 24 hours.
The A8 Soliwald tunnel at Brienzwiler, right on this route, is closed every night from 20:00 to 05:00 until 18 September. Be over the Brünig before eight and it is irrelevant.
The Turren cable car runs every 20 minutes and the last one DOWN on a weekday is 17:00. Do it in the morning or not at all.
The Half Fare Card buys nothing at the Aare Gorge - it is an attraction, not a transport tariff. It does halve the Turren, to CHF 18 return.
This is the day the alternative base would change. From LaVida Peak at Reichenbach the same drive runs about 25 minutes longer and lands you 66 km from Grindelwald Terminal instead of five minutes.

days.title: Jungfraujoch - Top of Europe
days.movement: Grindelwald Terminal sits down at Grund, five minutes from the apartment by road - bus 121 is free on the guest card. Eiger Express gondola to Eigergletscher, 15 minutes, then the cog railway through the inside of the Eiger to Jungfraujoch, about 25 more. Fifty minutes each way. First gondola 08:00, on the summit by about 08:50.
days.parents: Sphinx observation deck by lift - never the stairs - then the Plateau and the Ice Palace. Ninety minutes to two hours is plenty at this height, and then straight back down. Everything up there is indoors, level and lift-served.
days.adults: Get off at Eigergletscher on the way down and walk the Eiger Trail to Alpiglen: 6.5 km, about two and a half hours, almost all of it descending along the foot of the Eiger north face. Train back from Alpiglen.

per_person.item: Jungfraujoch return from Grindelwald Terminal, half fare

group.item: Grindelwald apartment + visitor's tax, night 2 of 4

tips: THE SEAT RESERVATION IS MANDATORY from 1 May to 31 October, so it applies today. CHF 10 a head, booked with the ticket at top-of-travel.jungfrau.ch. Without one the railway can simply be full. Be through the turnstiles ten minutes before departure.
THIS DAY FLOATS. Check the summit webcams at breakfast and go on the clearest morning of the four. Nothing else in the plan is ruined by cloud and nothing else costs this much.
Do NOT buy the Good Morning Ticket. It starts at CHF 190.40, it does not combine with a Half Fare Card, and it forces you off the summit by 13:17. The plain half-fare ticket is cheaper.

3,454 m, and the Sphinx deck is 3,571 m. About half of adults get a headache, dizziness or no appetite up here, usually two to twelve hours in - which is exactly why a short visit is the plan. Move slowly, drink water, skip the alcohol, take the lift.
September averages a high of 1 C and a low of minus 5 C at the top, before the wind. Coats, hats, gloves, sunglasses and sunscreen - the glare off the snow is worse than the cold.
The last half-hour of the ascent is inside a tunnel with no view at all. That is normal, not a fault.

Anyone with a heart or lung condition, sleep apnoea, or medication for either should ask their doctor before the trip rather than on the platform. There is a staffed medical room with oxygen at the top.
Confirm the exact last train down when you book. The published figures for September run between 16:47 and 17:47, and the difference decides how long you can linger.

days.title: Schilthorn, Piz Gloria and Mürren
days.movement: Drive to Lauterbrunnen, about half an hour, and park at the station. Ask for tariff D, the Rundreise via Grütschalp: funicular up the cliff to Grütschalp, the little shelf train along to Mürren, then cable car through Birg to the summit - and come back down the other side through Stechelberg. It costs exactly the same as the plain there-and-back.
days.parents: The shelf train from Grütschalp to Mürren is the loveliest flat ride in the Oberland - twenty minutes of Jungfrau across the valley with nothing asked of you. Piz Gloria turns a full circle while you eat. Skip the Birg walkways.
days.adults: Add the Thrill Walk at Birg, a catwalk bolted to the cliff face with open metal grating underfoot, and the Skyline Walk on the summit terrace.

per_person.item: Schilthorn round trip via Grütschalp, half fare

group.item: Grindelwald apartment + visitor's tax, night 3 of 4

tips: The Schilthornbahn rebuild is FINISHED - the last of the new cars was inaugurated on 2 April 2026 and there are no closures on these dates. This is the opposite of the Titlis situation.

Ask for tariff D. The circular route via Grütschalp and Mürren costs CHF 115 full and CHF 57.50 on a Half Fare Card - identical to the plain out-and-back - so there is no financial reason to do the same valley twice.
The last car off the summit is 17:50, reaching Mürren at 18:05. The last train Mürren to Lauterbrunnen is 19:58.
The Piz Gloria brunch needs a table reservation. It is not a walk-up.

Lauterbrunnen's multi-storey is CHF 18 for the day and connects straight to the station. Neither the operator nor the garage publishes a height limit, so measure the van before committing to it - Stechelberg, at CHF 7 for eight hours, is open-air with no limit at all.
The Thrill Walk floor is see-through. Some people find that far more unnerving than they expect, and there is no shame in taking the inside route.

days.title: Grindelwald First, Bachalpsee, and Harder Kulm at sunset
days.movement: The First gondola leaves from the middle of the village, and climbs in three stages, about 25 minutes. No driving in the daytime at all. In the evening the van goes down to Interlaken Ost for the Harder Kulm funicular - half an hour each way.
days.parents: The Cliff Walk at the top is included with the gondola: a level loop bolted to the rock with the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau lined up across the valley. Then the terrace at Berggasthaus First for lunch. Harder Kulm in the evening is a ten-minute funicular to a flat viewing platform - the most accessible summit in the whole region.
days.adults: Walk out to Bachalpsee: 3 km each way on a wide, gently rising path, about fifty minutes out and an hour and fifty round trip. On a still morning the Wetterhorn stands upside down in it. Come back down by trottibike if the legs are still willing.

group.item: Grindelwald apartment + visitor's tax, night 4 of 4

tips: The Cliff Walk is free with the gondola ticket. Do not let anyone sell it to you separately.
Harder Kulm runs to 21:10 in September and the ride is ten minutes, so it is an evening rather than a day. Save it for whichever evening is clear - it does not have to be this one.
Skip the First Flyer and the First Glider. Two- to three-hour queues are reported and the view is the same from the ground.
PACK TONIGHT. The Eidgenössisches Jugendjodelfest opens in Grindelwald tomorrow and you want to be gone early, not shuffling out through a thousand yodellers.
Bachalpsee is the one walk on this trip where the reward is completely out of proportion to the effort. If the parents are up for anything at all today, the first flat kilometre of it is worth doing.
If the day is washed out, this is the one to trade. Trümmelbach Falls, Schynige Platte and Blausee are all in the wet-weather list and none of them needs a summit.

days.title: Out before the Jodelfest, and back to Zurich
days.movement: Leave Grindelwald early. Down the Lütschental to Interlaken, the A8 along the Thunersee to Spiez and Thun, the A6 to Bern, then the A1 east to Zurich. About 155 km and a little over two hours. Van back at the airport by 12:00, refuelled. Then the hotel, and the afternoon is free.
days.parents: A quiet afternoon. The train from the airport into the city is 13 minutes, and the lake promenade and Bahnhofstrasse ask nothing of anybody.
days.adults: Same train, then the old town, the Lindenhof terrace and a swim off one of the lake badis if the weather has held.
tips: THE VAN IS DUE BACK AT 12:00. The hire is seven days from Saturday 09:00 and an hour late can bill as a whole extra day. Leave Grindelwald by 09:00 and there is an hour in hand.

The Jugendjodelfest takes over Grindelwald today - over a thousand performers, and the official line is no visitor parking in the village, use the park and ride at Matten. Another reason to be out early.
Refuel in Kloten town, not at the airport and never at a motorway services. The hire is full to full and the services charge the worst prices in the country.
The Kloten figure here is an estimate. Five people will not fit in two Zleep rooms - it is either three rooms or a family room somewhere else, and it is the last unpriced piece of the trip.
Nothing is booked for this afternoon on purpose. After four mountain days in a row, an empty half-day in a flat city is not a gap in the plan.

days.title: Zurich on foot, and the Knabenschiessen
days.movement: No van and no driving - it went back yesterday. The train from the airport into the city takes 13 minutes and runs every few minutes. The old town on foot all day, and the evening at Albisgütli.
days.parents: Lindenhof for the view over the roofs, the Fraumünster windows, and the lake promenade - all flat and paved, with somewhere to sit every hundred metres. At the Knabenschiessen: a funfair, food stalls and most of the city out on level ground, and you can leave whenever you like.
days.adults: Add the Grossmünster tower and the lanes behind Niederdorf. Then stay late at the festival - it runs to 01:30 and the trains keep going well past midnight.
tips: The Knabenschiessen is Zurich's own festival, 12 to 14 September, and today is the opening day. Free to walk into, and it runs until 01:30.
Tram 13 normally terminates at Albisgütli, but during the festival it stops at Laubegg, four minutes short. There is no visitor parking at all - which is one more reason the van went back yesterday.
Pack tonight, properly. Tomorrow's terminal time is 08:45 and it is not negotiable.
The shops inside Zurich main station open on Sundays, which almost nothing else in Switzerland does - useful if anything has been forgotten.
If the festival is too much after nine days, the lake boats run into the evening and the Old Town does not need a ticket.

days.title: Late morning flight home
days.movement: The hotel shuttle to the terminal. No van to return - it went back on Friday.
tips: Be at the terminal by 08:45 for the 11:45 departure. Flights to Tel Aviv carry extra security interviews and Zurich asks three hours for them rather than the usual two.
Check-in opens at 04:00 at the earliest, so there is nothing to gain by arriving before those three hours.

weather_swaps.do: Move the day. It is the only thing here that weather ruins outright and the most expensive ticket on the trip, and it is why the Tuesday floats across the whole Grindelwald block.
Boat down to Flüelen and back by train. Three hours through the dramatic far end of Lake Lucerne, all of it seated, none of it weather-dependent.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A washed-out day in the valley
weather_swaps.do: Blausee, down the Kandertal. A forest lake that still works in drizzle, with a 300 m flat asphalt path from the gate to the water and the glass-bottomed boat included in the entry. The Half Fare Card buys nothing here; a lunch reservation at the restaurant refunds half the admission.
Trümmelbach Falls. Ten glacier falls carved inside the mountain, reached by a lift built into the rock - but stairs beyond the halfway point and permanently wet underfoot, so adults only.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A wet morning in the Oberland
weather_swaps.do: Schynige Platte. A vintage cog railway from Wilderswil, a free alpine garden with over 750 species at the top, and noticeably fewer people than the famous peaks.
Harder Kulm. Ten minutes by funicular from Interlaken Ost, flat at the top, the classic two-lakes view - and it runs to 21:10 in September, so it fits after a mountain day rather than instead of one.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A day that wants a lake instead of a summit
weather_swaps.do: Oeschinensee above Kandersteg. Turquoise water under the Blüemlisalp walls, a gondola up and a 20-minute stroller-friendly path down to the shore, rowing boats and a toboggan run. An ascent time slot is MANDATORY from 20 June to 20 September and costs CHF 5 - without it you cannot board even holding a valid ticket.

The Niesen funicular from Mülenen, thirty minutes to 2,362 m on the pyramid that closes the end of the Thunersee. On Wednesday and Friday evenings the last descents run to 23:25, so dinner at the top is possible.

weather_swaps.instead_of: A spare mountain day with the parents
weather_swaps.do: Männlichen. Gondola up from Grindelwald Terminal and the cog railway down from Kleine Scheidegg, with the almost level Panoramaweg between them - the gentlest high ridge walk in the region.

booking_order: DONE - the Zleep Hotel in Kloten for Friday 4 September, the Historical apartment in Schwyz for 5-7 September, and the van: a 7-seat VW Caddy from Europcar, out Saturday the 5th at 09:00 and back Friday the 11th at 12:00.

The Jungfrau base, 7-11 September. This is now the tightest item in the plan. Chalet Adelheid in Grindelwald leads at CHF 1,356 for four nights, 4.99 from 165 reviews, a king and three singles, free parking for two cars and five minutes from Grindelwald Terminal. Chalet Waldhart at CHF 1,501 buys a second bathroom and free cancellation to 2 September. LaVida Peak at Reichenbach im Kandertal, CHF 1,474 flexible, is the fallback in the wrong valley.
Kloten for 11-13 September, for five. Two Zleep rooms will not hold five people - it is three rooms, or a family room elsewhere. The last completely unpriced piece of the trip.
Five Half Fare Cards, covering 4-13 September. Buy before leaving.

Jungfraujoch tickets AND the mandatory seat reservations, at top-of-travel.jungfrau.ch. Book once the week's forecast is readable, but do not leave it to the morning - the reservation is what gets you on the train.
The Piz Gloria brunch for Wednesday. The table reservation is required, not optional.
Nothing for the Saturday. The Knabenschiessen is free to walk into and Zurich's old town needs no ticket.
Nothing else. Rigi, Lungern-Turren, the Aare Gorge, Grindelwald First and Harder Kulm are all walk-up, and the Schilthorn tariff D is bought at the window on the day.

totals.note_vs_six: At six the shared costs barely move - the Grindelwald apartment, the van and the rooms at each end cost much the same either way - so the total would rise by about one more person's tickets and food while the figure each fell. Five costs less overall but more each. At six the luggage would not have fitted in the Caddy.
